question: How did criterion 2 get its final form?

revisions.statement: Selectivity (real - control) at the best layer
Selectivity (real - control) at the best layer

revisions.threshold: control's max balanced accuracy over layers does not exceed the 95th percentile of 10,000 redrawn mappings
revisions.note: A leak bound, not a selectivity floor: under a type-disjoint split the control task's ceiling is chance. Drafted as 0.50 ± 0.03 (b9c861b); replaced before the push because ±0.03 fires 59–80% of the time with no leak (61bf29e).

answer:
Criterion 2 went through three registered revisions.

**Revision 1 (commit 12a0349, 2026-08-22).** It began as a selectivity floor: selectivity (real minus control) at the best layer had to be ≥ 0.10 [crit-rev1-2].

**Revision 2 (commit c7323d0, same day).** The statement stayed the same, but the 0.10 threshold was marked "provisional" [crit-rev2-2]. The rows don't say why.

**Revision 3 (commit cb09c9d, 2026-09-26).** The criterion was reframed as "Control task shows no leak." It now passes if the control task's maximum balanced accuracy across layers does not exceed the 95th percentile of 10,000 redrawn mappings [crit-rev3-2].

The note explains the change. Under a type-disjoint split, the control task's ceiling is chance, so the criterion is a leak bound rather than a selectivity floor [crit-rev3-2]. The revision cites Hewitt & Liang 2019, §2.3 [paper-hewitt-liang].

Before the permutation threshold, there was an intermediate draft that was never pushed: control accuracy of 0.50 ± 0.03 (b9c861b). It was replaced because a ±0.03 band would fire 59–80% of the time even with no leak (61bf29e) [crit-rev3-2].

Each revision supersedes the one before it, so the leak-bound version (rev3) is the current form [crit-rev3-2].
